title: She Could Not Move for Fifteen Years, Yet Her Thoughts Lifted a Coffee Cup
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — Leigh Hochberg & BrainGate2 (2012): Paralyzed 15 Years, Cathy Hutchinson Drinks Coffee Using Her Own Thoughts and a Robotic Arm, grounded in Leigh R. Hochberg, Daniel Bacher, Beata Jarosiewicz, Nicolas Y. Masse, John D. Simeral, Joern Vogel, Sami Haddadin, Jie Liu, Sydney S. Cash, Patrick van der Smagt & John P. Donoghue (2012) (Nature, 485, 372–375). Empirical findings show that in 1996, a devastating brainstem stroke left Cathy Hutchinson (Participant S3, age 58 at testing) completely unable to speak or move her arms and legs (tetraplegia and anarthria), severing the neural highway between her intact cerebral cortex and her spinal cord while leaving her mind, vision, and motor intentions 100% awake.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how brainstem, motor cortex, parietal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that in late 2005, surgeons implanted a baby-aspirin-sized 4-by-4 millimeter silicon microelectrode array carrying 96 hair-thin 1.5-millimeter electrodes directly into the arm-and-hand knob of Cathy Hutchinson's primary motor cortex.

- Leigh R. Hochberg, Daniel Bacher, Beata Jarosiewicz, Nicolas Y. Masse, John D. Simeral, Joern Vogel, Sami Haddadin, Jie Liu, Sydney S. Cash, Patrick van der Smagt & John P. Donoghue (2012). - Leigh R. Hochberg, Mijail D. Serruya, Gerhard M. Friehs, Jon A. Mukand, Maryam Saleh, Abraham H. Caplan, Almut Branner, David Chen, Richard D. Penn & John P. Donoghue (2006). - Jennifer L. Collinger, Brian Wodlinger, John E. Downey, Wei Wang, Elizabeth C. Tyler-Kabara, Douglas J. Weber, Angus J. C. McMorland, Meel Velliste, Michael L. Boninger & Andrew B. Schwartz (2013).
